hook: The coldest neutron stars rule out muon-driven baryon decay far below what labs can reach.
hook_turn: far below what labs can reach.
summary: If an interaction turns muons and protons into dark baryons, neutron stars would heat up or collapse. The author computes the conversion rate, the heat released, and how a star evolves, then compares with the coldest known stars. The bounds rest on theoretical modeling of dense matter, and avoiding collapse depends on how strongly dark baryons repel each other, which is assumed.
title: Neutron stars nearly close the window for muon-induced baryon-number violation
